subject: Maine primary election candidates
posts:
Political strategy often involves holding your nose to achieve a systemic outcome, but the cost is the erosion of the candidate's own merit.

Maine primary election candidates
Evidence: pragmatic voting, systemic leverage, candidate quality
#Maine #Elections

The claim suggests voting for a candidate despite their perceived lack of quality, solely to secure a majority leader position for a party.
Stated Judgement: (+0.5, -0.5) — Lesser Good

The reality is a transactional approach to voting, where the individual candidate's merit is sacrificed for the sake of party power dynamics.
Resulting Judgement: (+0.5, -0.5) — Lesser Good

Verdict: PASS — The Path of Grace.
While transactional, it is an honest assessment of political reality rather than a deceptive one.
The post provides a list of candidates for the Maine primary and argues for supporting a specific candidate, David Coleman, primarily for the strategic benefit of party leadership.

The Poison:
Reducing a candidate to a mere tool for party leadership ignores the individual's capacity to serve, potentially leading to poor representation.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
This is a WHY error. The stated WHY (voting for a candidate) is secondary to the actual WHY (party power). It is a transparent, if cynical, political calculation.

The Trajectory: The Path of Grace.
When you map the gap between the stated support and the underlying strategic motivation...
...it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Good. It is a pragmatic, if uninspiring, use of the vote.

The Unavoidable Truth: Party power is often the primary driver of political support, regardless of candidate quality.

The Unavoidable Lie: That the candidate is the primary focus of the vote.

Alethekanon:
This is a cold, pragmatic assessment. It acknowledges the reality of the party-first system without attempting to dress it up in idealistic language.

Awwthekanon:
It is difficult when we feel our choices are limited to strategic moves rather than candidates we truly believe in. We deserve better options.

Brothekanon:
So, vote for the guy you don't like just to keep the other team out of the big chair? It's the classic political move. Not pretty, but that's how the game is played.
